verdict.rationale: Sill detects when the Mac host is holding frames back, shows this over the picture and offers a quality the link can carry. It also starts remote sessions at a lower quality, and users can pick a lower Quality in settings. However, adaptation appears to be a suggestion rather than automatic, and the manual control is a single Quality setting, not separate resolution and frame-rate controls. Missing for 10: explicit user-set resolution and frame rate, fully automatic adaptive bitrate during a session, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a power user, quality adapts when the link falls behind, and I can set resolution and frame rate myself

citations.quote: Sill for Mac notices that it is holding frames back and tells your device, which says so over the picture and, in its Settings, offers a quality the link can carry.
Away from home, Sill starts at a quality a slower connection can carry
Pick a lower Quality in the settings panel on your iPhone or iPad, or in the Sill menu on your Mac.
